newsitem.title: ITALY: Bertinotti says will back Italy govt on budget.
newsitem.headline: Bertinotti says will back Italy govt on budget.

text.p: The leader of Italy's Communist Refoundation party, which holds the balance of power in the lower house of parliament, said on Friday he had been misunderstood and confirmed his party would support the government over the 1997 budget.
Fausto Bertinotti was earlier quoted as telling Italian reporters after meeting Prime Minister Romano Prodi that his hard left party and the centre-left government were still not in agreement.
"There is still no accord. Our vote cannot be taken for granted," Bertinotti had said.
Bertinotti said later in a statement that his remark about the vote referred to the question of the establishment of a telecommunications watchdog authority
Bertinotti said both men spoke about a range of topics.
"I repeat that our judgment of the budget has not changed and, therefore, our vote in favour of it is not open to question," Bertinotti said in his statement.

The budget commission is the key lower house body looking at the package before it is presented to the full chamber next Wednesday. It is due for final approval in the lower house by November 14. It then moves to the Senate and must be passed by the end of the year.
